level_formula_check: Kingdra/Gyarados/Tentacruel offset 1 -> L83, Magikarp offset 0 -> L82, Raichu offset 2 -> L84. Confirmed.

attempts.narrative: T1 the AI switched Kingdra out for Raichu (a Lightning Rod read on the Thunderbolt), but Moonblast, aimed at Kingdra, hit Raichu instead and OHKOed it; Thunderbolt 4x OHKOed Gyarados. T2 Kingdra chose Rain Dance and was OHKOed by Moonblast first; Thunderbolt broke Magikarp's Sash and paralyzed it. T3 Tentacruel Protected both attacks; Magikarp Flail from 1 HP did 80 to Zapdos. T4 Moonblast KO Magikarp, Thunderbolt KO Tentacruel.

strategy_checks.check: Kingdra Rain Dance only when it repays
strategy_checks.evidence: T1 switched out; T2 native choice Rain Dance beside a Sashed Magikarp (the right time), KOed before moving. Rain never fell.
T1 native choice Waterfall; 4x Thunderbolt first.

strategy_checks.check: Raichu Fake Out + Lightning Rod hold the field, timed Mega
strategy_checks.evidence: Raichu entered by switch on T1 and was OHKOed on entry; Fake Out, Lightning Rod redirection and the Mega never happened.
T2 Sash held at 1 HP; T3 Flail did 80 to a 272 HP Zapdos. Swift Swim never mattered because rain never fell; as authored, spread damage or a paralysis (it was paralyzed by Thunderbolt) defuses it.
T3 Protect blocked Shadow Ball + Thunderbolt; KOed T4 before acting again.

protect_ledger.payoff: blocked Shadow Ball + Thunderbolt (lethal in sum); real

ai_observations: T1 Kingdra -> Raichu switch: a legitimate Lightning Rod read on Zapdos, but it put the team's only Mega and Fake Out user (4 HP EVs) into the line of a 2x Moonblast and it died without acting. Not illegal; costly.

level_changes.reason: won first try 5-0 with zero faints; Gyarados died before acting
same rule; one Protect then died. Magikarp (offset 0) left alone: the dossier says it is a novelty slot, not a scored set; Raichu is the Mega.

could_this_be_cooler: The joke survives contact: Sash Magikarp Flailed for 80 and it was the funniest thing in the block. But the rain never happened in this run, and the team's structure guarantees that against a fast Fairy/Electric lead: Kingdra is the only setter and it is slower than every good cap-84 special attacker. Giving Kingdra the lead beside Raichu (Fake Out buys the Rain Dance) instead of beside Gyarados would make the concept fire far more often without touching a set. Not changed in this pass.
